title: Pretraining Data Statistics Shape the Phases of Learning Entity Comparison in Language Models
claim: Models pass through distinct learning phases, relying first on frequency, then position, then the correct algorithm, at both small and large scale.
layout: 2 panels: left task example plus strategies, right stacked training-dynamics plots with shaded phases
description: Two-part figure. Panel (a), on the left, is a light-blue box with the question "Between France and Brazil, which country is larger?" The names are colored red and green. Beneath it are two bar charts, one for area and one for pretraining mentions. France is the red bar and Brazil the green bar. Brazil is larger by area, and France has more mentions. Below, a peach box titled "Candidate strategies" lists three rules: frequency gives France, first position gives France, and the correct algorithm gives Brazil. Panel (b), on the right, has two stacked line plots. The top plot is a small 163M-parameter LM over training steps. The bottom plot is OLMo-2 32B over pretraining tokens. Orange (frequency), blue (position) and green (correct algorithm) lines show the drop in accuracy when each feature is removed. Shaded background bands mark the three phases. The eye goes first to the colored bars and the green curves that rise late.
caption: (a) An example of the entity comparison task we use to disentangle the three candidate strategies. The task requires comparing the areas of two countries; the correct answer is Brazil in the given example. However, if the model relies on positional or frequency bias, it would predict France. (b) The importance of each strategy across training checkpoints, measured by the decrease in accuracy when the feature for that strategy is removed. The frequency heuristic (orange) is most predictive of LM behavior in the earliest checkpoints, but is quickly taken over by the positional heuristic (blue), and the correct algorithm (green) appears in late training. The three-phase structure appears in both the small controlled setting and the large-scale natural text pretraining setting of OLMo-2 models, up to 32B parameters.
abstract: How does data shape language model (LM) behavior throughout pretraining? We investigate this question through a case study on entity comparison, e.g., Between France and Brazil, which country is larger?, across nine comparison tasks spanning five entity types. We begin with controlled experiments in which we train small LMs (163M parameters) on mixtures of natural text from pretraining corpora and synthetic task data. Our analysis identifies three distinct phases of learning: (1) an early phase where the LM selects entities by frequency, (2) a middle phase where the LM selects entities by position in the prompt (first vs. last mentioned entity), and (3) a late phase where the LM selects the entity that is the correct answer. We show that the emergence of these three phases is causally determined by statistical properties of the training data. With small amounts of task-specific synthetic data, we observe only the first two phases and the model fails to learn the task; with large amounts, the model jumps directly from the frequency-based heuristic to solving the task correctly. Moreover, changing the entity frequency distribution from a naturally occurring Zipfian distribution (a small number of entities are very common and the vast majority are rare) to a uniform one weakens the frequency phase and speeds up learning of the task. Lastly, we show that the three phases of training dynamics from our controlled experiments appear in the open source model OLMo-2 32B. Together, our findings demonstrate that properties of pretraining data are causal drivers of heuristic learning and show that small-scale synthetic experiments can predict training dynamics at larger scales.
